newsitem.title: FRANCE: French inflation rise due to oil, cars - Treasury.
newsitem.headline: French inflation rise due to oil, cars - Treasury.

text.p: The rise in the year-on-year rate of French inflation in October was mainly due to higher oil prices and an increase in car prices as a government scheme to encourage car buying ended, the Treasury said.

National statistics institute INSEE said earlier on Tuesday French consumer prices rose 0.2-0.3 percent in October from September and climbed 1.7-1.8 percent compared with the same month a year earlier. Prices rose 1.6 in September compared with the previous year.
The Treasury said excluding energy prices the year-on-year increase was 1.3 percent. The cost of petrol products in France rose 2.4 percent in the month and climbed 10.8 percent year on year.
The Treasury also said the monthly rise in prices was affected by two seasonal factors moving in opposite directions. The cost of fresh food rose while the cost of some rail and train fares fell.
